4.evidence_source: Participants of the main study were 212 female and 241 male students from a university in Timis¸ County in the west of Romania.
4._section_summary: This section describes the main study (Study X): 212 female and 241 male university students in Timis County, Romania (total N = 453). Mean age was 23.57 years (SD = 7.86) and mean self-reported BMI was 22.18 (SD = 3.46). The sample were university students (72.2% undergraduate, 16.1% Masters, 11.7% other) and 97.3% self-reported Romanian ethnicity.

5.evidence_source: The test–retest sample consisted of 57 female and 52 male university students from the same university in the west of Romania.
5._section_summary: Study X: A test–retest sample of university students (57 female, 52 male; N = 109) from a university in the west of Romania; all participants reported Romanian ethnicity. Ages ranged 18–57 years (M = 25.02, SD = 8.91). Participants completed the BAS-2 at two time-points three weeks apart; no further demographics or BMI data were collected.

6.evidence_source: The results of the principal-axis factor analyses with the above subsamples point to a one-dimensional factor structure for Romanian BAS-2 scores, with all 10 items loading onto this dimension.
6._section_summary: This section reports factor-analytic and CFA results for the Romanian BAS-2, finding a one-dimensional factor structure with all 10 items loading on the factor. CFA performed on the second subsample (n = 243) required freeing three pairs of error covariances to reach acceptable fit (CFI = .950, RMSEA = .090, SRMR = .049); Cronbach's alpha for this subsample was .89 (95% CI = .87–.91).

7.evidence_source: The primary aim of the present study was to examine the factor structure of a Romanian translation of the BAS-2.
7._section_summary: This discussion summarizes a single study that evaluated a Romanian translation of the BAS-2, reporting a one-factor structure, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and expected correlations with related constructs. The authors note a lack of full sex invariance (configural and intercept invariance not supported), caution about generalizability due to a student (college) sample, and recommend further validation work in broader Romanian-speaking populations.
